name: Buick 320 cu in 'Fireball' straight-eight, Series 70 Roadmaster (1948-1950 specification; Dynaflow rating)
summary: Big, slow-revving 5.2 L overhead-valve straight-eight with a very long stroke, siamesed intake ports and a single exhaust outlet; peak power arrives at only 3600 rpm, so the sound is a smooth, low, even eight-cylinder hum rather than a V8 burble.

cylinders.note: '8 in Line', valve in head (pushrod OHV).

bore_mm.note: 3 7/16 in, converted by the researcher. Standard bore size 3.436-3.439 in.

displacement_cc.note: 320.2 cu in, converted by the researcher.

rod_length_mm.note: 8 1/4 in centre to centre (Series 70), read from the page image; converted by the researcher. Team Buick's summary table also lists 8.250 in.

compression_ratio.note: 1950 Roadmaster with Dynaflow. The 1948-49 shop manual gives 6.6 (Syncro-Mesh) and 6.9 (Dynaflow); the 1952 manual as transcribed by Team Buick gives 7.5 for the Series 70.

firing_order.note: Single bank. The pages read do not state which end is No. 1.

crank.value: Five main bearings, 114 lb crankshaft, laminated-steel flywheel-type balancer on leaf springs at the front; crankpin 2.248-2.249 in

bore_spacing.value: 4.075 in between cylinders 1-2, 3-4, 5-6, 7-8; 4.290 in between 2-3 and 6-7; 4.545 in between 4-5
bore_spacing.note: Contributor-supplied 'blue print' figures on Team Buick, not from the shop manual.

valves_per_cylinder.note: Not stated as a number; the rocker arm table lists one inlet and one exhaust rocker per cylinder (valves 1-8 inlet, 1-8 exhaust).

intake_valve_dia_mm.note: 1 25/32 in head diameter (Series 70), read from the page image; same figure in the 1950 specifications.

exhaust_valve_dia_mm.note: 1 7/16 in head diameter (Series 70); same in the 1950 specifications.

cam_timing_check_point.value: With No. 2 or No. 7 exhaust valve opened exactly 0.155 in (Series 70), the flywheel 'U.D.C. 1-8' mark should be at the timing hole
cam_timing_check_point.note: The only cam timing reference found: the shop manual's valve timing check (par. 2-18). It fixes one point on the exhaust lobe relative to top dead centre of cylinders 1 and 8; open and close angles are not given.

idle_rpm.note: Team Buick tune-up table, 1946-49 all models; the page notes Dynaflow cars need a higher idle.

peak_power_kw.note: 152 bhp bare engine, 1950 Roadmaster with Dynaflow, converted by the researcher. 1948-49 shop manual: 144 bhp (Syncro-Mesh) and 150 bhp (Dynaflow) at 3600 rpm. Wikipedia quotes 168-170 hp at 3800 rpm for 1952. These are gross (bare engine) ratings.

peak_torque_nm.note: 280 ft-lb bare engine, converted by the researcher.

intake_type.value: single carburettor on a cast-iron manifold feeding 4 intake ports (ports shared between cylinder pairs); intake manifold diameter 1 3/8 in, minimum intake port diameter 1 3/8 in
intake_type.note: 1950 specification table. Carburettor type and venturi size were not read.

runner_dia_mm.note: 'Intake Manifold Diameter' 1 3/8 in, Roadmaster, converted by the researcher.

header_type.value: cast-iron manifold with a single outlet (heat-control valve at the manifold outlet); straight-through resonance-type muffler
header_type.note: Single outlet inferred from 'Heat Control Location: At Exhaust Manifold Outlet' and a single tail pipe entry; the table does not say 'single exhaust' in words.

exhaust_pipe_dia_mm.note: Tail pipe 2 in outside diameter. Minimum exhaust port diameter 1 1/16 in.

missing: cam timing: intake and exhaust open/close angles and duration (only a single check point on the exhaust lobe is published in the shop manual pages read)
redline_rpm (no stated limit; power peaks at 3600 rpm)
which end of the block is cylinder No. 1
crank pin angles (pin layout of the straight-eight crank)
exhaust manifold branch dimensions and exhaust pipe (not tail pipe) diameter

sources.what: Scan of the 1948-49 Buick Shop Manual, Group 2 (Engine), on the Old Car Manual Project. Manufacturer service manual: general specifications, dimensions and fits tables for Series 40-50 and Series 70, valve timing check. Fractions were read from the page images because the PDF's text layer garbles them.
Hometown Buick '1950 Buick Specifications' page, a transcription of Buick's 1950 specification tables by series: horsepower, torque, compression, valves, manifold and exhaust data.
Team Buick reference page, 'directly compiled from the original 1952 Buick service manual' for the 263 and 320, plus contributor-supplied blueprint figures (rod length, bore pitch).
Team Buick tune-up table by year: idle speed, firing order.
Wikipedia overview: displacement table by year, 1952 ratings.

curb_kg.note: 'LWB Riviera Sedan ... Price : $2,740 ... Weight : 4220 lbs | 1914.16 kg'. The Henry Ford: '1950 Buick Roadmaster Sedan ... Weight: 4220 lbs' (https://www.thehenryford.org/collections/explore/artifact/163196). Neither says shipping or curb; the factory shop manual gives no weights. Model 72R chosen because it was the most built 1950 Roadmaster: 'LWB Riviera Sedan 4 dr. 6 P : 51,212' of 'Total 1950 Series 70 Roadmaster production : 75,034' (conceptcarz).

gear_count.note: Dynaflow: torque converter plus a planetary Low/Reverse; Drive is direct through the converter. 1950 manual p. 4-26 refers to a separate Dynaflow manual not online (https://www.teambuick.com/reference/library/50_shop/files/4-c.pdf).

gears.note: 1951 Buick Shop Manual p. 4-27: 'Torque Multiplication— Converter at Stall ... 2.25 to 1; Planetary Gears, Low and Reverse (ratio) .. 1.82 to 1; Converter at Stall and Gears in Low or Reverse ... 4.07 to 1' (read by a helper from the page image; the text layer confirms 4.07). Same figures in the TeamBuick Dynaflow manual, which says they 'can be generally used for all models' (https://www.teambuick.com/reference/library/dynaflow_napa/files/dynaflow_napa.pdf; 2.25 / 1.82 / 4.07 checked by me in its OCR). The 1951 unit is the same single-turbine Dynaflow as 1950 (helper's reading; twin-turbine came in 1953).

final_drive.note: 1950 Shop Manual p. 5-2, 'c. Rear Axle Ratios': '72, 76C, 76R ... Dynaflow ... 3.9 to 1 (43-11) [standard] ... 3.6 to 1 (47-13) [optional]' (checked by me on the page image). 43/11 = 3.909.

wheel_radius_m.note: No published rolling radius for the 8.00-15 tyre found.

tyre.note: 1950 Shop Manual p. 6-2: 'Tire Size (Except Mod. 79) ... [Series 70] 8.00"—15"'; rim 15" x 6.50"L (checked by me on the page image).

driven.note: English Wikipedia, 'Buick Roadmaster' (read 2026-11-17), infobox layout: Front-engine, rear-wheel-drive.
